 "traits": [
  {"id": 1, "label": "sloppy", "description": "This means doing the work fast and rough, skipping the checking, leaving loose ends, mislabeled figures and small mistakes, and calling it done."},
  {"id": 2, "label": "stream-of-consciousness", "description": "This means following natural thought patterns with spontaneous associations, tangential connections, and an unstructured flow from one idea to the next, rather than maintaining strict logical organization."},
  {"id": 3, "label": "methodical", "description": "This means working from a plan, step by step and in order, finishing each stage before starting the next, and sticking to the plan when something unexpected comes up."},
  {"id": 4, "label": "erratic", "description": "This means switching tone, approach and view partway through a conversation without warning or reason, so that no one can tell what comes next."},
  {"id": 5, "label": "meticulous", "description": "This means showing exceptional care for precision, accuracy, and thorough attention to every detail, being methodical and careful in approach."},
  {"id": 6, "label": "steady", "description": "This means holding the same tone, approach and view through a whole conversation. Any change of course is announced and explained, never a swerve."},
  {"id": 7, "label": "monochronic (from Edward Hall)", "description": "This means doing one thing at a time, organizing life around tasks, schedules and procedures, treating time as a thing to be saved, spent, wasted or lost, and keeping to the clock."},
  {"id": 8, "label": "distractible", "description": "This means having one's attention pulled off the task by every buzz, noise or passing thought, drifting mid-sentence and losing the thread."},
  {"id": 9, "label": "chaotic", "description": "This means living in a whirl of disorder: five things begun at once and none finished, plans and rules ignored, everything done out of turn, and confusion left behind."},
  {"id": 10, "label": "ADHD", "description": "This means a brain that cannot attend to what bores it: hours lost in whatever grips one, the dull task left to the last night, restless in a chair, school a struggle, better on one's feet."},
  {"id": 11, "label": "improvisational", "description": "This means working without a plan, taking each step as it comes and building on whatever happens, and making it up on the spot when something unexpected comes up."},
  {"id": 12, "label": "focused", "description": "This means keeping one's attention on the task through every buzz, noise or passing thought, and finishing each thing before turning to the next."},
  {"id": 13, "label": "company-loyal", "description": "This means staying with one employer from first job to retirement, never reading the job ads, and turning down every outside offer."},
  {"id": 14, "label": "polychronic (from Edward Hall)", "description": "This means doing many things at once, putting people and the business at hand before a preset schedule, seldom feeling that time is wasted, and hearing people out, schedule or no schedule."},
  {"id": 15, "label": "job-hopping", "description": "This means changing employers every year or two, always eyeing the job ads, and leaving the moment a better offer comes."}
 ]}

{"candidate": {"label": "organized", "description": "This means approaching every task step by step, sorting information into clear categories, and following a deliberate system so that nothing is left to chance or scattered across one's thinking."},
 "traits": [
  {"id": 1, "label": "learning-oriented", "description": "This means doing each task to get better at it, taking the hard problem over the sure win, and judging it by what one learned."},

  {"id": 5, "label": "focused", "description": "This means keeping one's attention on the task through every buzz, noise or passing thought, and finishing each thing before turning to the next."},
  {"id": 6, "label": "distractible", "description": "This means having one's attention pulled off the task by every buzz, noise or passing thought, drifting mid-sentence and losing the thread."},
  {"id": 7, "label": "logical", "description": "This means reasoning step by step from premises to conclusion, checking each inference, and refusing a claim that does not follow, however appealing."},
  {"id": 8, "label": "illogical", "description": "This means jumping to conclusions that do not follow, reasoning from how things feel or sound rather than from what has been established, and holding to an argument after its steps have been shown not to connect."},
  {"id": 9, "label": "methodical", "description": "This means working from a plan, step by step and in order, finishing each stage before starting the next, and sticking to the plan when something unexpected comes up."},
  {"id": 10, "label": "monochronic (from Edward Hall)", "description": "This means doing one thing at a time, organizing life around tasks, schedules and procedures, treating time as a thing to be saved, spent, wasted or lost, and keeping to the clock."},
  {"id": 11, "label": "expository", "description": "This means stating the point outright, defining terms, laying out facts, steps, and reasons in order, and never dressing information up as a story with characters, scenes, or plot."},
  {"id": 12, "label": "performance-oriented", "description": "This means doing each task to show how good one is, taking the sure win over the hard problem, and judging it by the score, not by what one learned."},
  {"id": 13, "label": "narrative", "description": "This means telling stories and using storytelling techniques such as characters, plot development, descriptive scenes, dialogue, narrative arcs, or dramatic elements to convey information."},
  {"id": 14, "label": "formalist", "description": "This means prioritizing structure, proper procedures, systematic organization, and adherence to established formats over flexibility, creativity, or a primary focus on content and substance."},
  {"id": 15, "label": "tactical", "description": "This means taking each problem on its own, making the direct move that wins it now, looking only at the small-scale problem and its immediate solution, and keeping no larger plan and no fallback."},
  {"id": 16, "label": "polychronic (from Edward Hall)", "description": "This means doing many things at once, putting people and the business at hand before a preset schedule, seldom feeling that time is wasted, and hearing people out, schedule or no schedule."},
  {"id": 17, "label": "improvisational", "description": "This means working without a plan, taking each step as it comes and building on whatever happens, and making it up on the spot when something unexpected comes up."}
 ]}
